feature: Reading & Writing half of the plan (their R&W sliders, 4 R&W focus domains, Reading/Vocabulary tasks, composite Score gap tile, RW/MATH accuracy legend, the 1,002-words stat card)
why_not_way_better: Their plan covers both sections: R&W current and target sliders, 4 R&W domains with Focus/Normal/Strong, Reading and vocab tasks, a total-score tile ('1000 now, 1400 target'), and Progress accuracy for both RW and MATH. Ours has an optional R&W number field on step 1, an R&W target field that appears only when that is filled, a free-text R&W own task, and Words. The Score tile, title ('Nov 7 · 700'), drift, pace, checkpoints and DomainCard are Math-only, so a student aiming for 1400 never sees their total. BankStats also drops their vocabulary stat, although we ship Words. A student using TTP for both sections sees half a plan. Decision 3 makes the site Math-first. It does not tell the plan to ignore R&W.
fix: Add an R&W block to step 1/2 and step 4. R&W current and target become sliders with number fields, not hidden optional inputs. Add the 4 R&W domains with Focus/Normal/Strong. Focus on Craft & Structure raises prefs.words_goal and SAT-word share. Focus on Expression of Ideas raises the transitions share. Each R&W focus domain adds a typed R&W own task titled by domain ('R&W · Standard English Conventions · 30 min'), with minutes split by the R&W shares. The Score tile, title, drift and Plans rows show Total when R&W is set. L11's Bluebook sheet records R&W misses per R&W domain. The DomainCard gets an R&W section fed by those logs. BankStats adds a Words tile (SAT words + transitions count, spaced review). All of it uses subject:'rw'.

feature: Task actions: Skip / Mark done / Practice again (theirs: visible buttons on the open task, a checkbox on every week row)
why_not_way_better: Theirs shows [Skip] and [Mark done] as buttons beside the launch button, [Practice again] and [Undo] on done tasks, and a 'Mark as done' checkbox on every week row. In ours (v2 3f, not overridden) Skip, Mark done and Again live only inside the ⋯ TaskMenu. Only own tasks get a real checkbox, and on phones the rest is keyboard-only or a long press. That hides one-tap actions theirs puts in view. It is below parity and breaks decision 4.
fix: On every TaskRow, show Skip (with L10's reason chips inline once tapped) and Mark done as visible quiet buttons next to Start/Resume. Make the status circle a real checkbox for every task, opening L10's 'Did it elsewhere?' form for question tasks. Show done rows' Again · the N you missed / Again · 10 more / Undo as visible buttons. Keep ⋯ for Move, Swap, Make it a section, Edit and Remove only.

feature: Decision 4: things collapsed or hidden to look lighter
why_not_way_better: The upgrade layout claims 'Nothing is folded away', but the spec still collapses many things. 'Why this?' is a disclosure, while theirs shows aiReason inline on week rows. The L15 changelog strip collapses to 'Updated this morning · 3 changes ›'. The Plans list collapses to 5 with 'Show all 12' (v2 3k and §6, not overridden). The 19 SkillRows sit behind DomainRow chevrons, even though skill focus is a headline extra. 'All 19 skills' is an expander. On phones, the L6 Live plan (the step-by-step selling point) is inside the Glance bottom sheet. Decision 4 says nothing useful is collapsed away or hidden to save space.
fix: Render the why lines inline under each task's detail line, always, with their L10 evidence links. Show the changelog lines expanded under the tabs, with 'No changes today' when empty. List every plan, paging by 20 only past 20 rows. Show SkillRows expanded under each DomainRow in step 4. Show the 19-skill table open on the Progress tab. On phones, render the Live plan (compact month, week 1, day 1 rows) inline above the sticky footer on every step, not in a sheet.

feature: Daily budget: L4 task order + L9 'Today I have' (their fixed durations and 'No day runs longer than you said')
why_not_way_better: The arithmetic doesn't close, so the headline 'plan you keep' breaks on the short days that matter most. Words is on by default (words_goal default 10, about 6-9 min). It is subtracted before q but is not in L9's shrink order. L9's stated floor (warm-up 3 + fix 4 = 7 q × 95 s = 11 min) already exceeds its own acceptance 1 ('≤ 10 minutes') before Words is added. Of L4's kinds 2-7, only pace, habit, learn and fix are trimmed. The warm-up (5, or 8 in Final) and the L3 check (4) are never trimmed, yet all of them must fit in 60% of q. On a 15-min day, q is about 6 while the fixed parts need warm-up 5 + fix 4 + check 4 + focus ≥5 = 18. Final's warm-up 8 + sweep up to 40% + focus ≥5 can exceed q. L9 also never says what happens to a test (35 min) when the student picks 10/15/30.
fix: Define one trim order covering every counted kind, including words, check, warm-up, sweep and test, and one floor per minutes value. For example, at 10 min: Words due-only capped at 3 min + warm-up 3, with fix moved to the next day. At 15 min: warm-up 3 + fix 4 + Words 3. Scale the 60% cap and the Final warm-up/sweep with q. When the chosen minutes are under 35 on a test day, move the test to the next day with ≥35 min and say so in the preview line. Rewrite L9 acceptance 1 so it holds for s = 95 with Words on, and add a check that for every chip value and s in 60-150 the counted minutes are ≤ the chip.

feature: L1 allocation: 'points decide the week' (v_t formula)
why_not_way_better: v_t = max(gain,2)/max(minutes,5) floors a mastered skill (gain 0, minutes 0) at 2/5 = 0.4. A high-value weak skill whose time-to-Strong is long, e.g. +20 needing 60 min (20/60 = 0.33), therefore ranks below a skill that is already mastered. The students with the biggest, slowest gaps get their most valuable skill deprioritised. That is worse than v2's (1.5 − m), which at least ranked weakness.
fix: Use v_t = gain_t / max(minutes_t, 10) for skills with gain ≥ 5. Give every other skill a fixed floor weight of 0.1 × the median v of the gain ≥ 5 skills, only so it stays in the deal. Add a __main__ assert that a skill with gain 20 and 90 minutes always outweighs a skill with gain 0.

feature: L1 Gate mode vs L2 hard-tier pins vs L5 difficulty
why_not_way_better: Gate mode (target > 580, m1 < 0.60) restricts Build and Sharpen to easy/medium, and L5 says Gate 'overrides Build and Sharpen'. L2 makes hard a needed tier exactly when target > 580, and guarantee 2 pins every needed shaky or untested cell twice before Final, through tiers_by_topic, which replaces tiers. For the gated learner the two rules contradict each other, and nothing says which wins. L1 acceptance 3 (tiers ⊆ {easy, medium}) can pass while tiers_by_topic still serves hard. As written, this can't be built.
fix: State the precedence: while gated, hard cells are not 'needed' (L2 counts hard as needed only when gate is off), and the gauge reads 'Hard tiers wait until your first modules reach 60%'. When gate turns off, hard pins go into the remaining Sharpen days, and a Final fallback pins them into the sweep if Sharpen is too short. Add an assert that no gated body carries hard in tiers or tiers_by_topic.

feature: L2 coverage guarantees (every skill every 14 days; every needed shaky/untested cell pinned twice before Final)
why_not_way_better: Slots are at most 3 per practice day. A new student has about 50 needed cells, so about 100 pinned slots. A 45-day plan's Build+Sharpen has about 25 practice days, about 75 slots. Guarantee 2 is infeasible, and even when feasible the pins take most slots, overriding L1's points allocation and the student's Focus. A 15-min, 2-days-a-week plan gets 1 slot a day, 4 per 14 days, so guarantee 1 (19 skills per 14 days) can't hold either. No cap, priority or fallback is given, and the acceptance tests only a generous synthetic plan.
fix: Cap pins at 1 per practice day and at most 30% of pre-Final slots. Order pins by the skill's gain (L1). Let pins ride inside a focus slot as a 2-question tier segment rather than consuming the slot. Scale guarantee 1 to 'every skill at least once per max(14, ceil(19 / slots per week) × 7) days'. Show unmet cells as 'not planned before Final' in the coverage card header. Add asserts for a 15-min × 2-day plan and a 45-day new-student plan.

feature: Verdicts on noise: L3 check pass on 3 of 4, L10 test-out 4 of 5, L13 per-checkpoint 'beat by 70' ✓
why_not_way_better: The v2 review threw out one-sitting verdicts because a ±70 band makes them flip on noise, then these upgrades bring them back. A student with a true 55% on a skill passes a 3/4 after about 39% of the time, and a 60% student passes the 4/5 test-out about 34% of the time. Both are then moved off Focus automatically (plan_auto_focus defaults on). A Strong skill gets 0.4 weight, so 'Slipping' takes weeks to collect the 12 answers that would catch it. Each checkpoint's 'beat by 70 / 20 under' and its WeekStrip ✓ judge a single sitting's midpoint inside its own ±70 band. That doesn't prove what the work fixed.
fix: A pass requires the After ≥ 3/4 AND at least 9 of the skill's last 12 clean first tries right at medium/hard (or 6-question before/after checks with ≥ 5/6). Otherwise it reads 'Again'. The test-out needs 8 questions with ≥ 7 right. Slipping keeps a 2-question keep-warm item per week on auto-promoted skills, so the 12 answers arrive. A checkpoint reads 'beat' only when the band's low end clears the aim, 'under' only when the high end is below it, and 'within the band' otherwise, with the ✓ only on 'beat'.

feature: L7 step 2 TargetNote ('700 ≈ 37 of 44 right' next to '88% of the section's points')
why_not_way_better: v2's review (D) removed '700 ≈ 39 of 44 right' as wrong because scoring is difficulty-weighted. L7 puts back U4's right_of_44 = round(44·F*), which is the same weighted fraction read as a question count, and prints it beside v2's '88% of the points' line. 44 × 0.88 ≈ 39, so the same note says 37 in one line and implies 39 in the next. It isn't honest, and it contradicts a correction already made.
fix: Drop 'N of 44 right' from the TargetNote. Show 'about 88% of the section's points' plus U4's skill list ('the points you're most likely missing are in Circles, Probability, Nonlinear functions'). If a count is kept, compute it at the learner's route tier mix (for example 'about 37 of 44 if your misses are mostly hard ones · 39 if spread evenly') with the weighting stated, and add an assert that the count and the points % agree.

feature: L6 landing example day with a live question, for a new student
why_not_way_better: There is no source for the question. L6 renders UI.workspace inline with T1's mode, but POST /api/plan/preview's sample_day returns Tasks with no {token, question}, and no call creates the session the answer is filed to. The example day also misrepresents the plan: a new student sees a blueprint-weighted focus set (v2 §6: 'focus starts on Algebra and Advanced Math'), but L7 makes 'Let the plan measure it' the default, so their real day 1 is the diagnostic followed by Map days. The 'see what a day holds before committing' claim is false for exactly the students it targets.
fix: POST /api/plan/preview returns first: {token, question} for the sample day's first question row, from T1's F5 preview path, and answering it creates a one-question source:'plan_preview' session. For measure-path learners, sample_day shows the real day 1 (Diagnostic · 20 q · ~30 min, then 'Map · 6 skills'), with the live question taken from the probe's first item. Delete v2 §6's 'focus starts on Algebra and Advanced Math' for measure plans.

feature: L8 Start today: 'the whole day in one run'
why_not_way_better: The run chains only drill or test blocks through plan.next. Words (a counted task on by default, launched at /api/words/run), homework assignments of kind module/section, and own tasks have no specified place in the run. The Words finish response doesn't carry plan.next, and nothing says whether the interstitial launches a words run. The day rail shows one segment per counted task, so a student finishing the run sees an unfinished rail and may not get 'Day done'.
fix: Order the run as warm-up → fix → learn/check → focus → Words → homework. Words runs as a block: the interstitial's next pane is 'Words · 12 due · ~6 min', Continue opens /words/ with run set, and words_finish returns plan {tasks, next}. Module/section homework opens the test lobby like a test block. Own tasks are listed as checkboxes on the final receipt and the rail marks them 'on your own'. Acceptance: with Words on, the run's last block is Words and the day ends done.

feature: L14 checkpoint twins 'compare like with like'
why_not_way_better: Between checkpoints, 'Fix these 6' drills exactly the slipped and still-missed slots' qids and templates, and the next checkpoint re-asks the same 22 templates. Checkpoints 'every 2nd test' on a weekly rhythm repeat the same 22 types 5-6 times in a 12-week plan. The '+90' and 'fixed 7' partly measure rehearsal of those 22 templates rather than skill. That is a quieter version of the retake contamination we criticise in theirs.
fix: 'Fix these' uses P18 siblings, meaning other templates of the same skill and tier (not the checkpoint's templates). Each slot records whether its template was practised since the baseline, and the card shows 'fixed 7 (2 practised)'. Alternate two baselines: the first module and the first fresh module of week 3. Label the series 'same question types' with a caveat line.

feature: L15 'What changed this morning, and why' + L20 changelog timeline
why_not_way_better: The snapshot stores only days (date, kind, minutes, test, topics, task kinds, counts). Causes like 'your edit, named', counts like '4 from your edits', and L20 lines like 'Oct 9 target 750' or 'Oct 2 fitted to 25 min' can't be derived from it: cfg PATCHes leave no history (plans.updated holds only the latest). Nothing stores the explicit lines L3, L7 and L17 are supposed to 'write'. Snapshots are taken only on the first GET /api/plan, so a student who works from Today (/api/today.plan) gets diffs spanning several days that are still labelled 'this morning'. As written, it can't be built.
fix: Add plan_events(plan, at, kind edit|auto|sitting|mistake|phase, field, from, to, text). Every PATCH, override, mark and auto change writes one row. Snapshot on the first plan.today_summary() or GET /api/plan of the local day, whichever comes first. The diff matches lines to plan_events for the cause, and the strip reads 'since Tue' when the previous snapshot is older than yesterday. L20's timeline reads plan_events.

feature: L18 'What your time bought' → Not moving flag
why_not_way_better: 'Under 3 points of change over its last 20 answers' is undefined: change against what, and how is it windowed? 20 answers have 5-point granularity, so the acceptance case '50% → 51% over its last 20 answers' can't occur. It can't be built or tested as written.
fix: Define it as: first-try accuracy of the skill's last 20 clean first tries minus the 20 before the plan start (or the first 20 in the plan), flagged when 60+ minutes in 14 days and the change < 10 points with at least 20 answers in each window. Rewrite acceptance 1 with 20-answer windows, e.g. 10/20 → 11/20.

feature: L19 taper vs exam-week test (their 'Exam day has arrived' with nothing changing)
why_not_way_better: The taper sets the last 5 study days to 0.6 × minutes (27 on a 45-min plan). A test needs ≥ 35 min, but v2 acceptance 2, which still stands, requires the exam-week module test on Thursday 2026-11-05, which falls inside the taper. L19 also says 'the last timed set 2 days out' (that Thursday) without saying whether it's the test. The rules and the acceptance checks contradict each other.
fix: State that in Final the weekly test is replaced by the dress rehearsal, so the exam-week test is dropped. Rewrite v2 acceptance 2 to 'the week of Nov 2 has no module test; Oct 31 is the rehearsal'. Make 'last timed set 2 days out' a 10-question timed focus set that fits the 27 minutes. Add an assert that no test lands on a taper day.

feature: Decision 3: subject-aware data (build additively for full SAT)
why_not_way_better: Only tasks get subject. The payloads keep a single subject each: points: {subject, ...}, coverage: {subject, cells}, score, projection, verdict, checkpoints and pace are single Math objects. cfg keeps Math current/target at top level, the 422 caps ('more than 2 domains') are global, and 'sections' is described as 'empty ['math']'. Adding R&W would turn each of these into a list or map and break every consumer, which is the tear-out decision 3 forbids when it costs little now.
fix: Key every per-section payload by subject now: points: {math: {...}}, coverage: {math: ...}, score: {math, rw?, total?}, projection: {math}. Store cfg.sections: {math: {current, target, focus, skills}}, with top-level aliases kept only for the learners mirror. Apply focus caps per subject (math: 2 domains / 6 skills). Validate unknown domains per subject.
